title: Four Oirats
capsule: The Four Oirats (Dörben Oirad) were a western Mongol confederation comprising the Choros, Torghut, Dörbet, and Khoshut tribes, attested here from 1402 to 1474. Under Esen Taishi (r. 1439–1455), grandson of Mahamu, the confederation reached its greatest power: Esen defeated and captured the Ming Yingzong Emperor at Tumu in 1449, extorted enormous ransoms from Beijing, and briefly claimed the title of Great Khan in 1452. Esen's assassination by rivals in 1455 shattered the confederacy's cohesion, and by the 1470s the Oirat groups had fragmented under renewed Eastern Mongol (Chinggisid) pressure, eventually reconstituting as the Dzungar Khanate in the seventeenth century.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Four Oirat territorial extent is largely conjectural steppe geography, reconstructed from Ming shilu records and Mongol chronicle sources; boundaries with the Northern Yuan and Ming frontier zones are approximate.
